Rashi on Ketubot 2b:10:1.english: And rather, from the latter clause - Rava derived that there is no [claim of] unavoidable accident in bills of divorce.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:10:2.hebrew: הרי זה גט - ואע"ג דאין אונס גדול ממיתה, אלמא אין אונס בגיטין, והוא הדין לחלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:10:2.english: This is a bill of divorce - And even though there is no unavoidable accident greater than death, evidently there is no [claim of] unavoidable accident in bills of divorce, and the same is true if he fell ill.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:11:1.hebrew: דלמא מת דוקא - דכל עצמו שכתב לה גט, מחמת כן כתב לה: שאם ימות יהיה גט למפרע, שלא תיזקק ליבם, ובהאי אונסא לא ניחא ליה למיבטל גיטא. אבל באונסא אחרינא, דניחא ליה לבטולי גיטא ביה, אימא לך: יש אונס בגיטין:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:11:1.english: Perhaps specifically [if he] died - For the entire reason that he wrote a get for her was on this account: that if he dies, it should be a get retroactively, so that she will not be bound to a yavam [levir]. And in this [case of] unavoidable circumstance, he does not want to cancel the get. But in another [case of] unavoidable circumstance, where he wants to cancel the get thereby, I might say to you: There is [a claim of] unavoidable circumstance in gittin.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:12:1.hebrew: ופסקיה מברא - הנהר הפסיקו, שהיתה המעבורת מצד העיר ולא יכול לעבור:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:12:1.english: And the ferry stopped him - The river stopped him, as the ferry was on the side of the city and he could not cross.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:12:2.english: See that I have come - [Meaning:] That I have come.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:12:3.hebrew: לא שמיה מתיא - והוי גיטא, ואם רצתה תינשא לאחר, וגם לכהונה נפסלת מהיום:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:12:3.english: This is not considered an arrival - And it is a [valid] bill of divorce, and if she wishes, she may marry another [man], and she is also disqualified from the priesthood from today.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:2:1.hebrew: פשיט רב אחאי - הך בעיא ממתניתין, דקתני לא נישאו ולא קתני לא נשאו, דלישתמע שהבעלים מעכבים:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:2:1.english: Rav Achai resolved - [He resolved] this dilemma from the mishna, which teaches: "They were not married," and does not teach: "They did not marry," which would imply that the husbands are delaying.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:2:2.hebrew: אלא לא נישאו - הן לבעלים, תלה העכבה בנשים:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:2:2.english: Rather, they were not married - [That is,] they [were not married] to the husbands; [the mishna] attributed the delay to the women.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:4:1.hebrew: ואיידי דתנא רישא בדידהי - נותנין לבתולה שנים עשר חדש, ולאלמנה שלשים יום:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:4:1.english: And since he taught the first clause with respect to them - [In the mishna:] "One gives a virgin twelve months, and a widow thirty days."

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:5:1.hebrew: ולענין גיטין אינו כן - אלפיכך קאי, דאשמעינן שעכבת האונס פוטרתו מן המזונות. לענין גיטין אין טענת אונס מועלת: אם נתן גט לאשתו ע"מ אם לא אבא עד זמן פלוני יהא גט, [ונאנס] ולא בא - הרי זה גט, ואינו יכול לומר: אנוס הייתי:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:5:1.english: And with regard to bills of divorce that is not so - [This] refers to [the statement beginning with] "Therefore" [above], which taught us that a delay caused by circumstances beyond one's control exempts him from [providing] sustenance. With regard to bills of divorce, a claim of circumstances beyond one's control is not effective: If one gave a bill of divorce to his wife on the condition, "If I do not return by such-and-such time, it shall be a bill of divorce," and he was prevented by circumstances beyond his control and did not return, this is a bill of divorce, and he cannot say, "I was prevented by circumstances beyond my control."

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:5:2.hebrew: אלמא קסבר אין אונס בגטין - אין טענת אונס בגיטין, ולקמיה מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:5:2.english: Evidently he holds that there is no unavoidable accident in bills of divorce - There is no claim of unavoidable accident in bills of divorce, and later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:1.hebrew: אינו גט - ואם אין לה בנים, זקוקה ליבם:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:1.english: It is not a bill of divorce - And if she has no children, she is bound to the levir.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:2.hebrew: מת הוא דאינו גט - דהא לא שויא גיטא עד י"ב חדש, והוא מת בתוך הזמן, ומאן קא מגרש לה מהשתא? אין המתים מגרשים:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:2.english: It is [only if] he died that it is not a bill of divorce - For it does not become a bill of divorce until twelve months [have passed], and he died within that time, and who is divorcing her now? The dead do not divorce.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:3.hebrew: מת הוא דאינו גט - משום דאין גט לאחר מיתה, אבל משום אונס אחרינא לא מפקע גיטא, אלמא אין אונס בגטין. דאי סלקא דעתך חלה נמי אינו גט, ניתני חלה, וכל שכן מת, שאין אונס גדול מזה:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:6:3.english: It is [specifically if] he died that it is not a bill of divorce - Because there is no bill of divorce after death, but due to another circumstance beyond [his] control, the bill of divorce is not voided; apparently, [the claim of] a circumstance beyond [one's] control does not apply to bills of divorce. For if it should enter your mind [that if] he fell ill, it is also not a bill of divorce, let [the mishna] teach [the case where] he fell ill, and all the more so [when] he died, as there is no circumstance beyond [one's] control greater than this.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:7:1.hebrew: היא גופא קמ"ל - כלומר, האי דתנא מת – לאו לדיוקא דילה תניה, למידק: הא חלה הרי זה גט, אלא לאשמעינן היא גופא: דאין גט לאחר מיתה. ואפי' בלא תנאי, כגון האומר לאשתו: הרי זה גיטיך לאחר מותי – אינו גט לפוטרה מן היבם:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:7:1.english: It comes to teach us this itself - Meaning, that which [the mishna] taught: "He died," was not taught for its inference, to infer: "Behold, [if he] fell ill, it is a bill of divorce"; rather, to teach us this matter itself: that there is no bill of divorce after death. And even without a condition, such as one who says to his wife: "This is your bill of divorce after my death," it is not a bill of divorce to exempt her from the levir.

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:8:1.hebrew: זה גיטך אם מתי - שכיב מרע שכתב גט לאשתו באחד מן הלשונות הללו: זה גיטך אם מתי, או זה גיטך מחולי זה – משיפסוק חולי זה (מעלי) משמע – והוא מת מאותו חולי, לא אמר כלום, שהרי משפסק אינו בחיים, ואינו יכול לגרש:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:8:1.english: This is your bill of divorce if I die - A person on his deathbed who wrote a bill of divorce for his wife with one of these formulations: "This is your bill of divorce if I die," or "This is your bill of divorce from this illness" — which means: "From [the time that] this illness ceases (from me)" — and he died from that illness, he has said nothing; for once it ceased, he is no longer alive, and he cannot divorce [her].

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:9:1.hebrew: דלמא - הא דאיצטריך סיפא אם לא באתי וכו', לאפוקי מדרבותינו איצטריך, דפליגי עלה ואמרי דאין גט לאחר מיתה הוא, דכיון דכתוב בגט זמן כתיבתו, הוא מוכיח שכך אמר לה: אם לא באתי לאותו זמן יהא גט למפרע מהיום. דאי לא משוה גיטא עד שנים עשר חדש, למה כתב יום כתיבת הגט בתוכו? לכתוב: אם לא באתי לר"ח פלוני יהא גט:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:9:1.english: Perhaps - That which the latter clause [of the mishna], "If I do not return, etc.," was needed, was needed to exclude [the view of] Our Rabbis, who disagree with it and say that it is not [a case of] a bill of divorce after death, for since the date of its writing is written in the bill of divorce, it proves that this is what he said to her: "If I do not return by that time, it shall be a bill of divorce retroactively from today." For if he does not make it a bill of divorce until twelve months [have passed], why did he write the day of the writing of the bill of divorce in it? Let him write: "If I do not return by such-and-such Rosh Chodesh, it shall be a bill of divorce!"

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:9:2.english: They permitted her to remarry - Without chalitzah, for that [woman in the case] of "If I do not come."

Rashi on Ketubot 2b:9:3.hebrew: זמנו של שטר מוכיח עליו - לא לחנם נכתב זמנו לתוכו, אם לא להודיע שמיום הכתיבה והמסירה הוא מגרשה, אם לא יבא לאותו זמן. הלכך, אע"ג דלא כתב זה גיטך מהיום אם לא באתי כו', כמאן דכתב מהיום דמי. ובבבא בתרא (דף קלו.) אמרה רבי יוסי, דתנן: הכותב נכסיו לבנו צריך שיכתוב מהיום ולאחר מיתה, ואם לא כתב מהיום אינה מתנה, רבי יוסי אומר: אינו צריך:
Rashi on Ketubot 2b:9:3.english: The date of the document proves it - Not for nothing was its date written into it, if not to make known that from the day of the writing and delivery he divorces her if he does not come by that time. Therefore, even though he did not write, "This is your get from today if I do not come, etc.," it is considered as though he wrote "from today." And in Bava Batra (page 136a), Rabbi Yose stated it, as we learned [in a mishna]: One who writes [a deed transferring] his property to his son must write, "From today and after death"; and if he did not write "from today," it is not a [valid] gift. Rabbi Yose says: He does not need to [do so].

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:11:1.hebrew: דלמא מת דוקא דלא ניחא ליה דתפול קמי יבם - וא"ת: בפרק מי שאחזו (גיטין דף עג. ושם), דאמרי' "אכלו ארי אין לנו" — פירוש: אין לנו שיהא גט — ואמאי לא הוי גט? הא לא ניחא ליה דתפול קמי יבם! וי"ל, דבאונס דלא שכיח כלל, לא אסיק אדעתיה שירצה שיהא גט:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:11:1.english: Perhaps specifically [if he] died, because it is not pleasing to him that she should fall before the yavam - And if you say: In the chapter [entitled] "Mi She'achazo" (Gittin 73a and ibid.), where we say: "[If] a lion ate him, we do not have [it]" — the explanation [being]: we do not hold that it is a get — and why is it not a get? Behold, it is not pleasing to him that she should fall before the yavam! And one can say: In [the case of] an unavoidable accident (ones) that is not common at all, it did not enter his mind that he would want it to be a get.

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:1:1.hebrew: מציא אמרה ליה נסתחפה שדהו - ואינו יכול לטעון דאדרבה מזלה גרם, דכיון דלא מיפקדא אפריה ורביה לא מיענשא, כדאמרינן בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סד:). ועוד, דהאשה היא שדה של הבעל, ואין הבעל שדה שלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:1:1.english: She can say to him: "His field was inundated" - And he cannot claim that, on the contrary, her [bad] fortune caused [it], for since she is not commanded regarding procreation, she is not punished, as we say in [the chapter] "HaBa Al Yevamto" (Yevamot 64b). And furthermore, the woman is the field of the husband, and the husband is not her field.

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:1.hebrew: פשיט רב אחאי - לא כמו שפירש רשב"ם, דהיינו רב אחאי גאון שעשה שאלתות, והיה בסוף כל האמוראים, ולכך משנה לשונו בכל הש"ס, פריך רב אחאי, פשיט רב אחאי; שהרי כאן רב אשי עונה על דבריו. אלא אומר רבינו תם שהוא אמורא, וכל אמורא היה תופס לשונו, כמו מגדף בה ר' אבהו (סנהדרין ג:), תהי בה ר' יוחנן (ב"ק קיב:), לייט עלה אביי (ברכות כט.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:1.english: Rav Aḥai resolved - [This is] not as Rashbam explained, that this is Rav Aḥai Gaon who authored the She'iltot and was at the end of all the Amoraim, and therefore [the Gemara] alters its phrasing throughout the Shas [to]: "Rav Aḥai objects," "Rav Aḥai resolves" — for behold, here Rav Ashi answers his words. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam says that he was an Amora, and each Amora had his own characteristic phrasing, such as: "Rabbi Abbahu scoffed at it" (Sanhedrin 3b), "Rabbi Yoḥanan was astonished by it" (Bava Kamma 112b), [and] "Abaye cursed regarding it" (Berakhot 29a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:2.hebrew: לא נשאו לא קתני אלא לא נישאו - מקובלין היו כך לקרות: לא נישאו. ועוד, דאי לא נשאו אאנשים קאי, ה"ל למימר נמי בלשון רבים: ואוכלות משלהם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:2.english: It does not teach "they did not marry," but rather "they were not married" - They had a received tradition to read [it] thus: "they were not married" (lo nise'u). And furthermore, for if "they did not marry" (lo nas'u) referred to the men, it should also have said in the plural: "and they eat from theirs" (ve-okhlot mi-shelahem).

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:3.hebrew: אלא לא נישאו - פירוש: דמשמע נמי דמעכבי אינהי. אבל אין לומר דמשמע דוקא דמעכבי אינהי, אבל לא אינהו, מדקאמר: לעולם דמעכבי אינהו, ואיידי דתנא רישא בדידהי כו'; דמשום איידי אין לשנות טעות בסיפא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:2:3.english: Rather, they were not married - The explanation is that it implies that they [the women], too, cause the delay. However, one cannot say that it implies specifically that they [the women] cause the delay, but not they [the men], since [the Gemara] states: "Actually, [it is a case] where they [the men] cause the delay, and since [the Tanna] taught the first clause regarding them [the women], etc."; for on account of [parallelism] (aydi), [the Tanna] would not teach an error in the latter clause.

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:6:1.hebrew: מת הוא דאינו גט - דאין גט לאחר מיתה, הא חלה הרי זה גט. דאי חלה נמי אינו גט, וטעמא דהכא דאינו גט משום אונס, אם כן, לישמעינן חלה, דהוי אונס מועט, וכ"ש מת; דהשתא אכתי לא אסיק אדעתיה, דבמת איכא למימר ניחא ליה דלא תפול קמי יבם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:6:1.english: It is [specifically if] he died that it is not a get - For [the reason it is not a get is that] there is no get after death, [implying that] if he fell ill, behold it is a get. For if [when] he fell ill it is also not a get, and the reason here that it is not a get is because of an unavoidable mishap (ones), if so, let [the Mishnah] teach [the case where] he fell ill, which is a lesser mishap, and all the more so [if] he died! For at this stage, [the Gemara] had not yet considered that regarding death, one can say that it is preferable to him [that the get take effect] so that she not fall before a yavam (levir).

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:7:1.hebrew: ודלמא לעולם אימא לך חלה נמי אינו גט - ויש טענת אונס. ודקאמר ליתני חלה וכ"ש מת, הא דקתני מת, הא קמ"ל: דאין גט לאחר מיתה; ואתא לאשמועינן תרוייהו: דיש אונס, ואין גט לאחר מיתה. דאי יש אונס גרידא אתא לאשמועינן, אבל יש גט לאחר מיתה, הוה ליה למינקט חלה; ואי אין גט לאחר מיתה גרידא הוה בעי לאשמועינן, לא הוה ליה למינקט הרי זה גיטך אם לא באתי שעושה תנאי, אלא הרי זה גיטיך לאחר מיתה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:7:1.english: And perhaps, actually, I could tell you that [if he] fell ill, it is also not a get - And [thus] there is a claim of unavoidable circumstance (ones). And as for that which [one might] say: "Let [the Tanna] teach [the case where he] fell ill, and all the more so [if he] died" — [the reason] that it taught "he died" comes to teach us this: that there is no get after death; and [so] it comes to teach us both: that there is [a claim of] ones, and that there is no get after death. For if it came to teach us merely that there is [a claim of] ones, but [that] there is a get after death, it should have stated [the case where he] fell ill; and if it wanted to teach us merely that there is no get after death, it should not have stated "Behold, this is your get if I do not come," which establishes a condition, but rather "Behold, this is your get after [my] death."

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:8:1.hebrew: הרי זה גיטיך אם מתי מחולי זה לאחר מיתה - לאחר מיתה הוי טעמא דכולהו, כמו: אתם ולא אפוטרופסין, ולא שותפין, ולא אריסין, ולא כל התורם את שאינו שלו (גיטין דף נב.), דכולהו הוו משום תורם את שאינו שלו. וא"ת: ההיא משנה גופה אמאי איצטריך? הא תנן בהדיא בפ"ק דגיטין (דף יג. ושם) דאין גט לאחר מיתה, דתנן: האומר תנו גט זה לאשתי, לא יתנו לאחר מיתה. ובפרק קמא דגיטין (שם ד"ה לא) פירשנו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:8:1.english: "This is your get if I die," "[if I die] from this illness," "[or] after death" - [The phrase] "after death" is the rationale for all of them, just like "[even as] you [are]" — and not guardians, and not partners, and not sharecroppers, and not anyone who separates terumah from that which is not his (Gittin 52b), for all of them are on account of [being] "one who separates terumah from that which is not his." And if you say: That mishna itself, why was it necessary? Behold, we explicitly learned in the first chapter of Gittin (daf 13a and there) that there is no get after death, as we learned: One who says, "Give this get to my wife" — they may not give [it] after death! And in the first chapter of Gittin (ibid., s.v. Lo) we explained [this].

Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:9:1.hebrew: דלמא לאפוקי מדרבותינו - אבל מההיא דרישא לא שמעינן לאפוקי מדרבותינו, דאיכא לאוקמה בשאין כתוב זמן בשטר. והא דאמרינן (בגיטין דף פו.) שלשה גיטין פסולין, וחד מינייהו שאין בו זמן, הא אמרינן אם נשאת הולד כשר; ומשום דאין גט לאחר מיתה, קתני הכא לא אמר כלום, אפילו נשאת. אי נמי, בשכתוב בו שבוע או שנה או חדש, דאמר בפרק שני דגיטין (דף יז:) דכשר, ואין זמנו מוכיח עליו. אי נמי, במאוחר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 2b:9:1.english: Perhaps to exclude [the view of] our Rabbis - But from that [case] of the first clause, we could not derive to exclude [the view of] our Rabbis, as it can be established where no date is written in the document. And as for that which we say (in Gittin 86a), "Three [types of] bills of divorce are invalid," and one of them is [a bill of divorce] in which there is no date, [where] behold, we say that if she remarried the offspring is valid — [yet] because there is no bill of divorce after death, it teaches here: "He said nothing," [meaning] even if she remarried. Alternatively, [the first clause can be established] where a sabbatical cycle, or a year, or a month is written in it, as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Gittin (17b) that it is valid, and [yet] its date does not prove [when] it [takes effect]. Alternatively, [it can be established] with a postdated [bill of divorce].
